Creates an empty backlog (TODO.md, archive.md, items/) in the folder, creating it if needed,
and adds it as a source. Refused with 409 backlog_exists if the folder already holds a TODO.md.

delete.description:
Moves the item in `version` to the trash and returns the items moved.

With children the answer is 409 has_children listing them; repeat with cascade=true to move them too.
Refused (409 item_referenced) while items outside the trash depend on it.

get.description: One item by id, active or archived.

patch.description:
Changes one or more fields of the item in `version`; all changes are checked and written together.

Completed/Rejected need a resolution and move the item to the archive.

get.description: A notes or spec document of the item, with its version.

put.description:
Replaces a notes or spec document in `version` with the whole new text.

With version null it creates `<ID>_notes.md` (first notes; the item needs a summary) or
`<ID>_spec.md` / `<ID>_spec_<topic>.md`. New dated notes entries: POST …/notes.

post.description: Appends a dated Discussed/Decided/Open entry to the item's notes (created on first use).

Changes the type of the item in `version`. The type is the id's prefix, so the item gets the next free id
of the new type, and every reference to the old id follows: parent and dependencies of other items, free texts,
notes and specs (their content and the items/<ID>/ folder). The answer is the item under its new id, the old
id, and notices: references outside the backlog (technical docs, daily reports, code, commit messages) are not
updated, so look for the old id there (notice external_references_may_remain).

Refused when the new type breaks a lifecycle rule (e.g. an epic with a parent) or the item is in the trash.

get.description:
The due notes of all projects with the reason, the topic path, the triggers that arrived, and the actions
that are possible, ordered by project and label.

schema.title: Response Due Notes Api V2 Notes Due Get

get.description: How many notes are due in all projects: a cheap call for the red exclamation mark.

Topics and notes with only label, status, due reason, review date, and summary: no long texts.

Without filters: the open notes of all projects. `project` keeps one project; `topic` (needs `project`) keeps
the notes in that topic and its sub-topics and the topics of that subtree; `status` is the effective status
(waiting, due, snoozed, done, dropped, promoted); `due=true` keeps the due notes; `linked_item` (in
`linked_project`, default `project`) keeps the notes that point at the item by a link or an event trigger.
`archived=true` reads the archive instead; a closed `status` does so by itself.
The global notes options.

put.description:
Changes the options sent and saves them in config.json; they apply from the next request on, no restart.

Topics that are nested deeper than a lowered `max_topic_depth` stay; only new topics and moves are checked.

get.description:
The notices of one note (`side=note`, `label` is the note label) or one item (`side=item`, `label` is the
item ID) in `project`, oldest first. With `open=true` only those nobody has decided yet.

schema.title: Response List Notices Api V2 Notices Get

post.description:
Decides an open notice. For a note: keep (the link stays, the review date moves), detach (the link to the
item goes), drop (the note is dropped); promote is not available yet. For an item: acknowledge. Answers with the
notice and, for a note, the note as it is now. Errors: notice_already_decided (409), decision_not_available
(409), version_conflict (409), notice_not_found (404).

A changed text sets a new review date unless `review_at` is sent. null clears `body`, `topic`, `review_at`.
Closed notes and notes in the trash cannot be changed (409 note_closed / note_deleted).

an item may be in another project (`target_project`). The same link twice is 409 link_exists.

post.description:
Moves the note to another project: it is created there with a new label (triggers, links, and documents come
along) and the old one goes to the trash. The answer is the new note; its `label` is the new one.
Appends a dated Discussed/Decided/Open entry to `<LABEL>_notes.md` (created on first use).

From the archive or the trash back to waiting, with a new review date. Refused (409 topic_deleted) while its
topic is in the trash.

Back to waiting with a new review date. Fired triggers are reset; a given `trigger` replaces all old ones,
and without it the triggers that cannot arrive again (time, topic) are removed.

Adds a trigger that makes the note due and returns the note. An event trigger also links the note to the
item; if the item has the status already, the trigger fires at once and is marked `already_met`.

A topic with sub-topics or notes needs `cascade=true`; they go with it. Otherwise 409 topic_has_content lists

Moves the topic with its subtree below `parent` (null: to the top).

Refused when it would make a loop (400 topic_loop) or the subtree would exceed the depth limit

schema.title: Response List Sources Api V2 Sources Get

post.description:
Copies all data of a database project between the database and its sync folder (`sync_path`).

Without `confirm` this is a preview and changes nothing: what is created, what differs (`changed`: the target
is overwritten) and what the target has that the origin lacks (`missing`), plus a `token`. With `confirm` and
that token the sync is carried out; if either side changed since the preview the answer is 409 sync_stale.
Missing entries are deleted only with `delete_missing`; otherwise they stay and are listed under `kept`.
Errors: sync_path_missing (400), sync_same_backend (409), sync_source_invalid (400, `details.reason` names the
problem, nothing was changed).

get.description:
Which side of a project with a mirror changed since its last sync (a sync through this API).

Computed when asked, not with the lists of projects: it reads both sides of the project. Changes nothing and
syncs nothing. `unknown` means never synced while the sides differ, `unreadable` that a side cannot be read.
Type, location (no password) and schema version of the central database; read-only.
`GET /sources/{id}/sync-status` for every project, in the order of the projects.
